chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Ghālib ibn ʿUthmān, from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, peace be upon him, who said:
Whoever controls himself when he desires, when he fears, when he craves, when he becomes angry, and when he is pleased, Allah will forbid his body to the Fire.

key_terms.إِذَا اشْتَهَى: at the time of craving or appetite
key_terms.إِذَا رَغِبَ: at the time of desire or inclination
key_terms.مَلَكَ نَفْسَهُ: restrained and governed his own self

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about controlling desire, fear, and anger?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches mastery of the nafs in changing emotional states, especially desire, fear, anger, and contentment. It presents self-restraint as a path of salvation, with the promise that Allah will make such a person's body forbidden to the Fire.
